en: Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 14.18. The Dyad on the Outflows:
That which is dissociated from the outflows and that which is subject to the outflows.

Dependent on a state dissociated from the taints (*āsava*) that is itself subject to the taints, there arises a state dissociated from the taints that is not free from the taints, by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

Dependent on a state dissociated from the taints that is free from the taints, there arises a state dissociated from the taints that is not free from the taints, by way of root-condition … three [combinations].

Dependent on both a state dissociated from the taints that is subject to the taints and a state dissociated from the taints that is free from the taints, there arises a state dissociated from the taints that is not free from the taints, by way of root-condition.
In the case of the root condition, there are five; in the object condition, two ... [and so on] ... in the non-disappearance condition, there are five. (The full detail applies in all cases.
The Chapter on the Taints is finished.
